SBP: If you would rather an issue be addressed in a later block, let us know and we can document this preference in the minutes.
Only in the case that someone’s physical or mental health is in imminent danger will we opt to disclose a student’s identity to an appropriate resource.
You can file an ATM report with your name or anonymously, based on your preference.
If you would like for a report to be filed on your behalf, we are available for that as well.
If an issue arises with personnel please quantify the number of students who felt this way and get concrete details if possible (as the student is comfortable)
Did you feel you were put in a situation where you didn’t have adequate supervision?

Please follow up on any topics or student comments in which you feel you need more information to lead the group to actionable specific feedback to deliver to the clerkships.

Are there other issues with the learning environment (“curricular events”) which may not meet the definition of mistreatment but may raise concerns for a student. Curricular events refer to concerns that occur during medical student specific didactics or teaching events outside of the clinical environment
ICS: First, this session is entirely anonymous and what is said here, stays here.
You will be able to see what I write to make sure you are comfortable with it.
However, if you are more comfortable talking one-on-one about issues, you can approach us after the session, as we will stay in the room for an additional __ minutes to be available to talk.
If you have experienced mistreatment during this rotation and would like to file an ATM report or need help finding resources for support, we can help guide you.
Describing specific behaviors and giving concrete examples is important so that the CD and/or MEO can both identify the specific issues and fix them.
If you are not comfortable answering our follow up questions, that is fine, just please let us know.
As we scribe, please feel free to suggest edits to what we are writing so we can capture your feedback in a way that is both accurate and comfortable for you.
Rather than asking for agreement, check for disagreement. Do this by asking, “Is there anything anyone wants to change about our ground rules?”

It is important to note when the conversation is deviating from its goal (e.g. to when students are focusing more on the assessment form than on mistreatment). You can call it out or move on to the next prompting question to try to head back to your structure/regain focus.

When a student has brought up an uncomfortable experience and is met with resistance sometimes it is best to air on the side of legitimizing and validating that experience. Then follow it up by pushing the group to come up with their own solutions.
